cohort: The study included patients from the Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology Clinic Outcomes Reporting System database who underwent their first frozen embryo transfer (FET) resulting in live birth, categorized as those with recurrent pregnancy loss (cases n = 3,299) or a comparison group with tubal ligation (TL) only (n = 1,408).
finding: Patients with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss undergoing frozen embryo transfer (FET) do not have an increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes compared to patients without infertility or RPL.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in mode of delivery between patients with recurrent pregnancy loss and the comparison group who underwent frozen embryo transfer.
